question: John Young jumps and salutes. What is the gravity on the Moon?

report.answer: John Young crouches, leaps and salutes by the flag. Tracking his backpack through the airborne phase (frames ~15-68) fits a near-vertical projectile with g ≈ 1.85 m/s², consistent with the known lunar 1.62 m/s² and ~5x below Earth gravity — which is why he hangs in the air so long.
assumptions: Camera is still and motion is roughly in a vertical plane facing the camera
Scale from the jumping suited astronaut itself: 1.9 m tall ±0.12 m, at same depth as motion
Fit uses frames 15-68 airborne phase to avoid crouch/landing articulation; scale uncertainty folded into error bar

forks.why: Show ~5x lower apex and much shorter hang time for same launch speed

forks.why: Hang time and apex intermediate between Moon and Earth
